chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Sharif ibn Sabiq al-Taflisi, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra al-Samandi. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
There was a famine among the Children of Israel, to the point that they exhumed the dead and ate them. Then they exhumed a grave and found in it a tablet upon which was written:
"I am so-and-so the Prophet. An Abyssinian will exhume my grave. What we sent ahead — we found it; what we ate — we profited from it; and what we left behind — we lost it."

key_terms.بني إسرائيل: The Children of Israel — used in Islamic tradition to refer to the ancient Israelite community as a moral exemplar
key_terms.فلان النبي: So-and-so the Prophet — the anonymity emphasizes the universality of the wisdom, not the identity of the prophet
key_terms.لوح: Tablet, board — a physical inscription found in the grave, bearing prophetic wisdom
key_terms.ما أكلنا ربحناه: What we ate we profited from — the only worldly gain that translates to real benefit is what one personally consumed or enjoyed
key_terms.ما خلفنا خسرناه: What we left behind we lost — accumulated wealth left at death brings no benefit; it becomes a loss
key_terms.ما قدمنا وجدناه: What we sent ahead we found — referring to charitable deeds or good works invested in the afterlife
key_terms.مجاعة: Famine, severe hunger — the desperate context that led to the extreme act of consuming the dead

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about wealth and charity through the story of the Children of Israel?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) relates a story about the Children of Israel during a severe famine, in which they resorted to exhuming and eating the dead. Upon opening one grave, they found a tablet bearing an inscription from a prophet, which contained the famous wisdom: deeds sent ahead in charity are preserved, what one consumes is their real gain, and what is hoarded and left behind is lost. This hadith teaches that charitable spending in this world constitutes the only true gain in the afterlife.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
